I bought No Man's Sky at launch and was hugely disappointed in it, but still enjoyed the relaxing wander through weird looking planets in an art style that I really liked. Hello Games deserves much praise for what they have turned their game into. It feels like a completely new and different game. The story feels more driven, and with greater interaction with the player. The overall content with the factions and the quests feels a lot more in depth, although more types of quests would be nice. The addition of land and ocean vehicles is absolutely the best change that the game has seen. It makes traversal a lot easier and more fun at times. I love the space anomalies as well, although some of them could do with some actual functionality rather than just an interesting looking object. I love the hub that the Space Anomaly has become, seeing the ways in which people design their characters and the ships they choose is fun, although I often accidentally interact with a player instead of a vendor. 

I do have a couple of major gripes with the current build though: The terrain manipulator doesn't seem to work with flattening land, and there is nothing worse than coming back to the base you spent hours building only to have it be literally underground. The electronics system could use some more options as well. I hated building a full base without the ability to see electronic fields yet, then discover that later in the game my base sucks power like nothing else, and my array of solar panels could barely keep up. Additionally, the wiring being permanently visible is extremely frustrating for visual design. the capacity to make it invisible would be greatly welcomed.

I haven't mentioned everything that I like and dislike about the game, that would be too long of a list. I would happily recommend this game at this stage to anyone that loves the idea of space exploration and the odd grind for materials and/or credits. With all that it offers one could easily spend hours and hours in this game, and even though I have finished much of what is available in terms of story, I jump back in whenever I just want to relax. I think this game deserves all the love it has been getting recently and I can't wait to see what Hello games decides to do in the future.

I figured I'd give this game 24 hours of play to finally comment on it.

No Man's Sky is an exploration game based off a procedurally generated universe containing about 18 quintillion planets. Each planet has it's own type of atmosphere, hazards, colors, flora, and fauna. The same proceduarl algorithm controls, the ships, weapons, and looks of each of the 3 main races in the game, the Gex, the Korvaxx, and the Vy'Keen. They have different personality types and each one that you converse with will have best ways to talk to them with varying rewards/penalties for doing the right/wrong thing.

You start out on a planet with a broken ship and are tasked with fixing it and setting out to explore. Your multitool doubles as a mining beam and weapon and can be upgraded with various attachments gained through mining and crafting. You'll swap your tool for better ones all throughout the game.

Your suit also has upgradeable components and you'll be spending plenty of time working on adding slots and giving it better mobility and protection upgrades.

My biggest complaint is that inventory management takes a bit too much of my time. I'd have to spend time transferring inventory from my suit to my ship and vice versa. Rarer items don't stack, so you can carry very few of them, even after you've maxed out your slots.

The interface is slow as well. Seems like it takes a bit longer to zoom in and out of the various mini-cinematics when it saves the game.

The variety in game is very nice, but everything tends to have a similar look. When you see one particular dinosaur creature in one solar system, you might find another one even with similar colors minus arm feathers in another. I'd definitely like to see some more variety, but I'm literally only 24 hours into the game so far. 

There are things to do, and an overarcing storyline which you can follow if you want some guidance. It's interesting and pertinent to what you're doing.

I do recommend this game if you love to explore. It's not a game for people who love the fast paced action of Call of Duty or Battlefield, but this game has much more surface to touch on than either of those titles. I've definitely gotten my money out of it already and I've only just dropped into it. Think Space Skyrim/Fallout with less personal choices...

Edit: Addendum to this review. The game KEEPS getting better due to the steady flow of FREE megacontent updates. There is now MORE in this game than the original trailer promised, and yes, that includes giant worms.

Reviews.208168:
[u]Updated Review[/u]

Update: I gave the game another try after the origins update, and it is surprisingly fun now that they have added multiplayer. There are still loads of bugs but there is a lot of content to play.  I've now had over 90 hours of gameplay time so I feel like I've got my money's worth, although I would recommend getting it at a minimum of 50% discount. 

Below is my original review:
-------------------------------
So I ignored all the naysayers and all the negative reviews and bought this game on the very first day. The price was a bit steep at $90 NZD but I figured I would get atleast 90 hours of enjoyment if not more.

I was having fun racing to the centre of the galaxy until a few revelations:

* The game is pointless. Once you reach the centre of one galaxy, all it does is teleport you to another galaxy with ALL YOUR TECH BROKEN DOWN. So you have to repair *all* of it.

* All the names of the creatures that you named are wiped off the server every two weeks, apparently.

* Every time you purchase a new ship, your current one is literally written off. It's entirely worthless. 

Heck, even Endless Sky, which is free, does a better job of being a space sim than this game. Definitely wouldn't recommend spending $90 NZD for it.

[u]Orginal Review[/u]

This game fills a void left by Freelancer ages ago.

It's everything I expected. Well there are a few bugs here and there, and some improvements to be made in the UI. The graphics too could be better, and at $90 NZD it's not cheap.

In saying that, the art style is pretty good.

Explore star systems. Land on planets. Land on moons of planets. Mine. Trade. Manage Inventory. Explore. Analyse. Shoot. Explore. Make enough money to buy a new ship. Repeat.

Oh, there's a storyline too, but you can follow it at your own pace.

After playing for 14 hours (not visiting every single planet), I finally landed on a Paradise planet, with islands and beaches all around. It was indeed a remarkable feeling.

Okay. I will start of saying this: I was hyped for this game. And I still am. I immediately cranked out almost a dozen hours playing this game, and I enjoyed every second of it. No ounce of the hatred and loathing for this game that was surrounding me in the media effected me enjoying this game at all. Exploring, and NAMING THINGS in a game where you can travel across stars and galaxies. The IDEA for the game in itself is amazing, but I do have some doubts about how the game will be in a few years. 
As of right now, there are game-breaking issues such as crashing, FPS lag, etc. I have not experienced any of the following until today, which encouraged me to write this review. 

I love the idea of No Man's Sky, and I love just about everything about this game. No multiplayer when there was said to be multiplayer annoys me slightly, but I won't just stop playing the game or flame about it because of it. Perhaps if the crashing, and fps issue were fixed and there was a slight optimization of the game, more people would enjoy it. 

A few reviews of this game said that the combat was "lack luster" which I don't necessarily disagree with, but this game isn't about combat per se. It's an exploration game, not a FPS combat-based game. 


TDLR: I love this game, despite it's issues. Not everyone is into games like this, which is fine, but they should not buy the game, play it for 1 hour and then trash it on forums. 

Definitely needs some optimizations and patches to fix crashing and FPS issues, but otherwise it runs fine (If you havea  decent PC) 

As for the multiplayer aspect: Maybe Hello Games will release a form of multiplayer in a future patch. If they don't, then that's fine. I will still enjoy this game to the fullest. 

Not everyone will enjoy this game, so keep it in mind. 

*Edit in 2020: This game has overcome alot and Hello Games has brought their vision to life. Multiplayer, dlcs, etc. This is a Labor of Love and I've nominated it so.

I was one of the original preorderers way back even before the delays. I actually preordered the game the first day preorders opened. I had a countdown on my phone, I had the wallpaper, I had the news alerts, I had everything. On release, this was one of the most disappointing games ever. Nothing was there. The galaxy was dead. The game in my head -- one with massive culture systems, fully unique planets, and deep experiences -- was gone. Four years later, it's still gone. But what's in its place is finally a good game.

Modern No Man's Sky is a fully enjoyable experience. It has some bugs, it has some jank, but the experience of landing on a planet is still interesting every time. There are concrete things to work toward with real weight to your actions. The game is, to save words, fun. Just know the first act takes around four long hours of planet shuffling, but after that, the freedom and openness of the game makes it, if still not what was advertised, fun. It's a good game. Buy it on sale.

Updated 20/11/2020:
What changed...
The graphics are worse. Constant texture pop in & outs. 
The audio is a mess, sounds levels are inconsistant with ear blasting loud sounds randomly occuring.

***ORIGINAL REVIEW***
Where to start.... I should mention despire a few freezes at times I had no issues with frame-rates, only a few crashes and no problems using Alt-Tab while in the game.

The Good:
The graphics are good.
I can be quite fun once you figure out what you're doing.

The Bad:
Console controls with no attempt to adapt them to keyboard & mouse.
Some of the settings seem to reset or just have no effect (music volume & controller vibration).
Inventory space is tiny and items that should stack dont.
Some of the quests are buggy.
The game needs auto-run.
The Planets are all the same (*).
The creatures all sound the same (*).
The Plants are all the same (*).
The locations are all the same (*).
The UI.

The Ugly:
The controls are bad, really bad.

The UI:
The UserInterface while clean and simple is also awful. Information frequently appears partly off-screen. The same happens when comparing Multi-Tools & Ships.  Achievements or Milestones (and saves or meeting people to a lesser extent) are annoying as they prevent you from using most keys in what feels like an attempt to make up for the lack of cut-scenes or just a pathetic try to make the game feel cinematic or artistic. Just show a badge on screen and don't break immersion. Tips and dialogs show the default key not whatever you changed it to. Some contact with alien races requires a certain level of friendship but the game doesn't tell you which you are. Its like asking someone to pick a number from 1 to 3 but giving them the choices blue, green or red.

The Controls:
I've been playing with move/look sensitivity at 20 and yet moving the mouse quickly still spins you around. Any lower and slow mouse movement feels like you're steering a cruise ship. It makes combat (especially space combat) incredibly annoying. On planets the game aim-assists so shooting in an enemie's general direction will hit your target requiring no real skill. Stamina is really limited but although you can increase it theres no point. Its almost impossble to run for any useful length of time as any time the terrain drops over 4mm you'll stop sprinting (which requires 2 button presses).  Menus are a complete mess. The mouse cursor resets position when changing between inventories or pages of a list. Some interactions require a click, others require you to hold the button down while the cursor animates a circle once (or twice sometimes). Controls that should be a single keypress with a keyboard are just simply mapped to the equivalent keys.

(*) I should clarify. Sure some planets are red-ish, green-ish or brown-ish and some have grass, others have water and so on but the layout is all the same. They all have the same kinds of caverns, the same kinds of rock structures and the same kind of terrain. The same can be said for the plants, animals and locations you find. Theres a small amount of variation (maybe 8 or 9 types) but they all start to look the same after a while.

In summary:
While technically a remarkable idea and potentially a very good game the piss-poor controls ruin immersion and make the game annoying. The level of grind is insanely high and you'll be doing a hell of a lot of boring mining/exploring to earn money.  It can be fun to play but I feel once the novelty wears off the samey feel to everything will get very old very quickly. Wait a few months until they fix things or until the price drops below £20.

AT RELEASE review:

I went into this game with only one expectation and that was limitless exploration. NMS has knocked that out of the park. The scale of this game is unbelievable and impressive for such a small dev team. Here's my quick points:

Pros:
1.) It really does feel limitless.
2.) Learning alien languages word by word helps feel like you're progressing.
3.) Several viable ways to earn in-game cash, with numerous ships and upgrades available to buy.
4.) *Once you're in the game* The content loads seemlessly, no load screens or hang ups.
5.) Having a dogfight in space which plummets into a low atmosphere chase was one of the coolest things I've done.


Cons:
1.) Its price. I agree with most people that this game should be maybe 20-25 dollar range, so wait for a sale.
2.) Optimization: The settings are strange. I have a GTX 970 and can run at or above 60fps on medium. **Important: This game starts with a 30 fps lock!! You need to manually set your frame cap to 60 for good visuals**
3.) A few bugs which need to be patched.

Overall I give this game a recommendation, but realize its meant for a niche market of sandbox explorers.

EDIT: After spending more time since this review (maybe like 7 more hours in game) the flaws really start to stand out. The absolute lies we were told by the developers about content that is in the game** isn't actually in the game.

Do not buy this game at full price. Do not buy this game for a while, until they've released patches that have the content we were promised in the base game.

Also, paid DLC expected?? Are you kidding me Hello Games???

January 2021 Update: Game is very good now, worth the buy. Tons of content, functioning multiplayer, quest lines, etc.

What can be said about No Man's Sky that wasn't said already? I mean your either in Boat A or Boat B. The game was either too hyped up that it failed to meet the critical standards the fanbase built for it. Or you are in your own head about it and see the game for what Sean and crew said it would be.

"A mind-bendingly large journey through billions of scaled planets, all created within an algorithm that I don't even know what it'll make."

Is this the world stopping best game of all time? Nope. Is it a commercial flop like Spore? Nope. Is this game boring an repetetive? Depends on playstyle. Now, the game is what it is. An immense journey through the stars with a definitive focus on exploration, scanning, and scavenging. There isn't a whole ton to do initially other than run inventory management and gather credits to upgrade yourself. The game focuses on keeping you busy by running around and seeing the planets. The more linear players only see this as hapless grinding. That's not a bad outlook, but it's also not the only one. You can spend an entire hour wandering around a cave system without ever leaving just staring in awe of what the games generation created. Love it or hate it, the game is an indie gem and a success story, reviews aside.

Check out the first Episode of my Twitch Stream of the game for a look at it!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BSkhluILW6M

2020 edit: Hello Games has continued to support the game by constantly adding content into the game at a rapid fire pace. They have transformed this game into a work of art that thousands and thousands of players enjoy exploring on a nightly basis.

Original review:

While the game is fun at first, after a few dozen planets you'll start to realize the game, with all its trillions of planets, is in fact pretty empty.

At best, you'll be upgrading your ship, suit and weapon/tool for a few planets and after that it's a gind to get to .. well, nothing. There is nothing at the end of the story except the story itself which is quite poetic but without much real player involvement.

If you are unlucky, you've already upgraded almost everything at the first planet and there's hardly anything to do for the remainder of the game.

Add to that, the fact that promised features are NOT in the game. There is absolutely no interactive multi-player support, you can NOT meet up with other players! Portals don't seem to do anything, you can NOT fly through canyons, there are no special ship types, no real factions.. at least not in a way that it matters, and the ending is quite unfulfilling.

It's also a very easy game once you've got a few upgrades. Too easy. Getting the upgrades is also too easy.

Creatures are funny to look at but nowhere near what was shown in the trailers. They are also not very intelligent and seeing hordes of wild life being hunted by other wild life never happens. And a lot of them look stupidly unrealistic. No logic behind their build-up. Juist some random number generator adding body parts left and right without any thought behind viability. Maybe it was intended as being a joke. In that case, it's spot on.

The only pro this game has in my opinion, is the art style. It is beautifully retro as was commonly used in scifi cover pictures in the 70's and 80's. Both space and planets are very colorful and can create extremely beautiful surrealistic views. This makes the game excellent for slow paced exploration. But that's really all there is.

Combat is very simplyfied. Galaxy map is horrendous to navigate. There are no planetary maps, no big space fights, no factions to fight for except saving some freithers and getting rep for one of the three races which in the end.. does nothing.

On the occasion of the Fall 2020 Autumn Sale event, four years after I gave this game an astoundingly mediocre review, I nominate this game for....

THE PENULTIMATE LABOR OF LOVE. (upgrade from the 'crash and burn' Icarus award.)

This game was always a proverbial diamond in the rough, but credit to Hello Games, they diligently worked their collective indie butts off to bring this game to the Stanley Kubrickian standard of sci-fi ultimate adventure fantasy polish.

A great game that recovered amazingly from its infamous rough start. The devs listen to what the fans want and have released buttloads of content and systems since launch, all for free. Recently they (FINALLY) released a generation overhaul which improved the variety in the procedural planets and creatures. I was looking forward to this update a lot; I was originally drawn into NMS by the promise of amazing sights and strange worlds, so was naturally disappointed at the palette-swapped worlds and body-part-swapped animals we had on the game's release.

Since the update, I've definitely seen more interesting worlds, flora, and fauna than I was used to, though to my chagrin they didn't reset any pre-existing planets' terrain, they only added one or two planets with the new terrain generation code to each star system. Of course, they did this to avoid terrain issues with planets where people had settled and built, but I wish they had at least changed the generation on pre-existing but undiscovered planets since that literally couldn't have harmed anyone and would have brought more diversity to the universe.

There are also a surprising amount of bugs still in the game. Me and my friends experienced some instability, crashes, strange occurrences like not being able to see each other while playing together, and some bugs that we remember from the game's early days that still somehow haven't been addressed.

Despite my convoluted nitpicking and the bugs, No Man's Sky is still great. Hello Games continues to support it and make it into the game they and fans always wanted it to be. It's only going to get better with time, and I look forward to seeing how it continues to grow.

Reviews.223367:
Four years after release I have come back to update my review and... it's so sad how broken this game is.

They did SO MUCH to add content to this game, making for some really interesting progression, but the endless stream of bugs destroy any fun that is to be had. Most of these bugs are probably specific to multiplayer, but I can't say for sure.

* You put resources in refiners... and they just disappear
* You try to take stuff out of the refiner, and you can't
* You build structures, and they disappear (your spent resources are gone, though)
* You return to a base you built hours ago... and half of it is gone
* You get stuck while trying to land on uneven terrain
* Your friends in multiplayer can become invisible
* You are unable to talk to some quest givers in multiplayer, forcing you to switch to single player to continue your game before joining back in with your friends.
* You fire a mining laser from an exo-vehicle and it appears in front of all your friends even though you are miles away from them.

Within about 10 hours of playing the game with friends, we collectively probably restarted or reloaded the game about 30 times, and we probably spent about 2 of those 10 hours figuring out bugs or re-grinding things that we lost due to bugs.

Some of these bugs were there at release release (before multiplayer was even in the game).
Some of these bugs have been there since multiplayer came out.

If there is one thing this game does well, it's VR. If you own a VR headset, get this game and play it in single player. You will have a hoot. But only because there are so few good VR games, that this actually quite medicore VR experience is still one of the best.

The worlds do look good but after the awe feeling goes away they really are just boring, lifeless, repetitive procedural generated boredom with creatures doing nothing as opposed to the trailers and same lil collection of buildings looking the same and giving the same things with nothing interesting happening really. Your suit, ship and multitool becomes nothing then a grindfest just to upgrade them with new slots so you can hold more materials which you can trade in their so called so deep trading system so you have credits to buy new stuff which have more slots so that you hold more stuff and rinse and repeat.
